feed.title: [BIP Proposal] Wallet label synchronization (BIP-329 records over encrypted stores)

entry.title: [BIP Proposal] Wallet label synchronization (BIP-329 records over encrypted stores)
entry.summary:
The discussion about integrating a general specification for inter-wallet communication addresses several key aspects that are crucial for the development of such standards. The proposal emphasizes the importance of considering a broad scope that would encompass various use cases like PSBT sharing, multisig setup, and payment confirmations. This approach is aimed at ensuring that wallet developers do not need to implement different transport and synchronization methods for each type of inter-wallet data format.
In the realm of design decisions, the ideas of deterministic discovery, merge semantics, and transport agnosticism are highlighted as having significant merit. These concepts could potentially streamline the process of inter-wallet interactions by creating more standardized procedures for discovering and merging wallet data across different platforms without being tied to a specific transport protocol.
However, there are reservations about adopting Nostr as the reference transport for these interactions. The critique centers on Nostr’s prioritization of censorship resistance, which might not align with the paramount need for privacy in financial data sharing. Instead, alternatives that emphasize privacy, such as ephemerality and OHTTP, are suggested as more appropriate due to their focus on enhancing user privacy in data exchanges.
Additionally, the development of a Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) for canonical output descriptors is mentioned, which could further influence the standardization efforts in wallet communications. For more insights into these discussions, the original thoughts and detailed explanations can be found in the linked message on a forum dedicated to Bitcoin development: [BitcoinDev discussion](https://groups.google.com/g/bitcoindev/c/GTIO4xDX5MU/m/-MoPJhiTAwAJ). This link provides access to more comprehensive arguments and technical details regarding the propositions mentioned.
